clue.text: Lyrics regularly displaying good sense

indicators.note: regularly shows every second letter of the words good sense, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A songwriter's lyrics praised for showing good sense now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so lyrics in the plural is a fair synonym.

clue.text: For the present, a row ultimately about European border

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word about

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A dispute about where a European frontier lies, settled only for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately about' gives only T, the last letter of about, rather than a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning meanwhile or temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Director's an international artist

parts.note: a player picked for their country wins a cap, so an international can be called a cap
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stock abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A film director described as an artist known around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'. Frank Capra directed It's a Wonderful Life.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Capra was a celebrated Hollywood film director of the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: Fancy meeting you here — in Lilliput?

definitions.meaning: the stock remark made on bumping into an acquaintance somewhere unexpected
Lilliput in Gulliver's Travels is a land of tiny people, where everything is little in scale

explanation.surface: A surprised greeting on meeting someone in Swift's land of tiny people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom people say on an unexpected chance meeting; literally it describes the miniature land.

clue.text: Mammal going after Prince Harry

indicators.note: the mammal follows the prince's letter, so it is placed second

parts.note: an otter is an aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: An animal trailing behind Prince Harry, perhaps on a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince Harry' reads as one royal, but Prince gives only P and Harry is the boy wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J. K. Rowling's novels, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Leading man Balls was obtrusively conspicuous

parts.note: the leading man of a film is its star
Ed Balls is a British former Labour politician and TV presenter

explanation.surface: A star actor named Balls who made a show of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a former British cabinet minister, later known from Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense of the verb stare is to stand out glaringly, to be too visible.

clue.text: County town girl, coming out, reversed car

indicators.note: reversed says the letters for the girl run backwards

parts.note: a debutante, a deb, is a girl making her coming-out into society
Ford is a car make

explanation.surface: A debutante leaving a county town and backing her car out.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDFORD is the county town of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Each English county has a principal administrative town; this is the one for Bedfordshire.

clue.text: Perhaps lie by a medieval castle's outer wall

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of lie by a could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Possibly someone would lie beside the outer wall of an old castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailey is the outer wall, or the courtyard it encloses, of a motte-and-bailey castle.

clue.text: Tips up public ballot boxes

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
votes are cast into urns, an old name for ballot boxes

explanation.surface: Someone upends the ballot boxes at a public election count.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip up something is to upset or capsize it, the same as knocking it over.

clue.text: Cast plays?

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay is a set of letters spelling acts, then out, a sign to rearrange them, which yields cast

explanation.surface: A one-word question asking whether the cast are the ones who perform plays.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'ACTS' with 'OUT' as an anagram signal, and it produces the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To act something out is to perform it, as actors perform or play out a scene.

clue.text: Send out publication

definitions.meaning: to distribute or release something officially
a single edition of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispatch a newly printed magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a verb for distributing and as a noun for one printed number of a periodical.

clue.text: One-star review by Her Majesty provokes storm from a particular direction

indicators.note: to review is to go over again, here read as rework the letters of one-star

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen's one-star review causes a royal storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' looks like the critic's verdict, but it is the anagram signal on One-star.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale blowing in from the north-east, especially on the US Atlantic coast.

clue.text: More than one being present, I tie shoelaces inside

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the run present, I tie shoelaces

explanation.surface: Someone present explains that they are tying shoelaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is one entity, a thing with its own existence; the plural matches more than one.

clue.text: Athenian character shows up in Guatemala

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit within the word Guatemala

explanation.surface: A Greek visitor appears in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows up' reverses UAT, found in GUATEMALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character of Athens' script.

clue.text: See 4
Extraordinary starter of whelks and poached flounder

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter of the word whelks
poached, as cooked, means the letters of flounder are mixed

explanation.surface: A seafood menu: whelks to start, then a poached flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonderful means remarkable, out of the ordinary, a near synonym.

clue.text: Experiencing difficulties, hits one up for change

indicators.note: for change says the letters of hits one up are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble lands a punch to get out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in trouble or a mess is being in a tight spot.

clue.text: An unaired gag, reworked prior to seasonal finale — for spirit (with 19?)

indicators.note: reworked means the letters of an unaired gag are rearranged
the finale is the closing letter of the word seasonal

explanation.surface: A comedy writer reworks an unused joke before the Christmas special's ending.
explanation.walkthrough: '(with 19?)' hints the spirit has WINGS, 19 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective spirit thought to watch over a person, traditionally pictured with wings.

clue.text: See 23
Former secret police section stopping circulation of claret?

parts.note: the Stasi were the secret police of East Germany

explanation.surface: East German agents stopping a wine's distribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a stoppage in the flow of a body fluid such as blood, so a halt in circulation.

clue.text: Band's victory songs ignoring the 10

parts.note: a victory is a win

indicators.note: ignoring says the letters for the 10 are left out of songs

parts.note: 10 Across is ISSUE, and issue means offspring, a son

explanation.surface: A band celebrating victory with songs, while ignoring the tenth one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 10' refers to 10 Across's ISSUE, in its sense of offspring, giving SON. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wings was the rock group Paul McCartney formed after the Beatles.

clue.text: Period in musical when tenor's substituted note

indicators.note: substituted says one letter takes the place of another in the musical's name

parts.note: Wicked is a stage musical
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A period in a musical where a tenor is swapped in for a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when tenor's substituted note' means T put in place of D.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a wicket can mean the span of a batting partnership, a stretch of play.

clue.text: Dickinson's last verse about butterflies

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the poet's name Dickinson
about, as in moved around, means the letters of verse are rearranged

explanation.surface: Emily Dickinson's final poem, on butterflies.
explanation.definitionFit: Having butterflies in the stomach means feeling anxious, a fit of jitters.

clue.text: Once money's disregarded, bell-ringing party's most important

indicators.note: disregarded says the letter for money is ignored and removed

parts.note: a chime is a ringing of bells
a fest is a festival or party

explanation.surface: Once cash is set aside, the bell-ringers' party is what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after party is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefest is an old superlative of chief, meaning foremost or principal.

clue.text: See 4
Fellow having left, festive charm's cultivated one night

indicators.note: cultivated, as in worked over like soil, says the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: With a man gone, festive charm is put on for one evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' says F is taken from the letters of festive charm's before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names one particular evening, the twenty-fourth of December.

clue.text: For instance, taking time to pause

indicators.note: taking says the word for example takes in the time letter

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, like for instance

explanation.surface: An example of a moment taken to stop and rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a halt or postponement, as in a stay of execution.

clue.text: Drops everything in empty factories

indicators.note: in says the word for everything sits inside
empty leaves only the outside letters of factories

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Production falls in factories that stand empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Falls and drops are synonyms, as verbs or as nouns for descents.

clue.text: Falsehood obscuring French leader's biography

indicators.note: obscuring says the lie wraps round and hides the leading letter

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word French

explanation.surface: Lies hiding the truth in a French president's biography.
explanation.definitionFit: A life is a written account of someone's history, as in 'Lives of the Saints'.

clue.text: Glance over upon hearing Hieroglyph cry

indicators.note: upon hearing means the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: Hieroglyph is the setter, who refers to themselves as I; to bawl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick look at the setter on hearing a cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters call themselves by their pseudonym; here Hieroglyph gives I, and I-BAWL is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is informally to look it over or scrutinise it.

clue.text: Film and detailed 26 — upset in the end, James Stewart elates

parts.note: Up is a Pixar animated film

indicators.note: detailed means cut off at the tail, losing the final letter

parts.note: 26 Down's answer, meaning biography

indicators.note: upset turns those two closing letters upside down, so they are read in the other direction
in the end takes the final letter of each of the words James and Stewart

explanation.surface: A film review of James Stewart's life, said to cheer audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset in the end' makes ST into TS; 'detailed' clips LIFE to LIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To uplift people is to raise their spirits, to cheer and buoy them.
